context.instructions: `item.text` is one architecture decision record as JSON. Does its context name the problem and the forces behind the decision?

criteria.problem and forces: Names the problem and the forces or constraints that shaped the decision.
criteria.background only: Gives background but no problem. Fix: state the problem.
criteria.missing: No context in substance. Fix: add the problem and its forces.

alternatives.instructions: `item.text` is one architecture decision record as JSON. Does it name the alternatives considered?

criteria.named with reasons rejected: Names alternatives and why each was rejected.
criteria.named only: Names alternatives without why they were rejected. Fix: add why rejected.
criteria.none: Names no alternative. Fix: add alternatives.

consequences.instructions: `item.text` is one architecture decision record as JSON. Does it name the decision's consequences?

criteria.positive only: Names only benefits. Fix: add the costs.
criteria.missing: Names no consequence. Fix: add benefits and costs.

d_ctx_gap.instructions: `item.text` is one architecture decision record as JSON. What is the context section most missing?

criteria.nothing: It names the problem and the forces.
criteria.problem: A statement of the problem being decided.
criteria.forces: The forces or constraints pulling against each other.
criteria.mixed: It mixes context with the decision itself.

d_alt_gap.instructions: `item.text` is one architecture decision record as JSON. What is the alternatives section most missing?

criteria.nothing: Each alternative is named with why it was rejected.
criteria.reasons: The reason each alternative was rejected.
criteria.alternatives: Real alternatives (only straw men or none are listed).
criteria.link: A link from each rejection reason to a force in the context.

d_cons_gap.instructions: `item.text` is one architecture decision record as JSON. What is the consequences section most missing?

criteria.nothing: It names positive and negative consequences.
criteria.concrete: Concrete effects (it is abstract or restates the decision).
criteria.separation: A clear separation of positive from negative consequences.

d_cons_weak.instructions: `item.text` is one architecture decision record as JSON. Which consequence statement is weakest?

criteria.vague: One uses a vague word (simpler, better, cleaner) with no measure.
criteria.restates: One restates the decision instead of an effect.
criteria.unowned: One does not say who or what is affected.
criteria.speculative: One is speculative (may, might) with no condition.
